basis: spec/layers/09-data-store.layer.json description: the data-store layer's modelling rules (maintainer decisions 2026-11-06), with Context Studio's 24 data-store proposals judged against them

actions.note: optimizes was used once, for an index and the access pattern it serves; the pattern uses the index (the relationship is reversed by its triple rule)

containment is one level at a time: a database composes namespaces (or collections and views directly), a namespace composes collections, views, stored logic and namespaces, and a collection composes its fields, indexes, validation rules and event handlers; namespaces contain collections, so the relationship is reversed (Context Studio op 21, which proposed dropping it)
one predicate per meaning between a pair: reading records to check them is accessing them (Context Studio op 1)
stored logic does not group fields; it accesses the collection that holds them
a validation rule is a declarative schema object of its collection, not part of procedural code (Context Studio op 10)
an access pattern names the key, sort and filter fields it uses; it does not contain them (Context Studio op 2)
one predicate per meaning between a pair: a pattern targets an index, it does not contain it (Context Studio op 24)

one predicate per meaning between a pair: behaviour uses the structure that serves it, so the reversed twin folds onto accesspattern uses index and optimizes, used only here, is retired (Context Studio op 4, which proposed keeping optimizes instead)
an event handler fires on the data change in its collection, not on the request that caused it
the store reaches the business layer through the application layer and the data model: stored logic realizes application functions, collections realize business objects (Context Studio op 9)
one predicate per meaning between a pair: an event handler is attached to its collection, which composes it, so the relationship is reversed onto the existing type
a handler raises the application event; the business event is reached from it, not from the store (Context Studio op 5)
a rule names the fields it constrains; it does not contain them

stored data is passive: collections, views, fields and databases are accessed, referenced and mapped, and never serve or trigger; the rule constrains the field, so the relationship is reversed (Context Studio op 17, which proposed stored logic aggregates field, a different pair)

stored data is passive: collections, views, fields and databases are accessed, referenced and mapped, and never serve or trigger; a column-level trigger names the fields it watches, so the relationship is reversed

stored data is passive: collections, views, fields and databases are accessed, referenced and mapped, and never serve or trigger; stored logic is started by an event handler, which references the field (Context Studio op 8, which proposed event handler triggers event handler)
